metadata.title: Omni Model Clean High-Density Cinematic Taxonomy
metadata.description: Zero-URL, dense cinematic taxonomy engineered specifically as modular style ingredients for Gemini Omni video generation.

genres.name: Wuxia Swordplay Fantasy
genres.description: Mythic martial artists defying gravity across bamboo groves and mist-shrouded temple rooftops, embodying philosophical chivalry and fluid swordplay.

genres.name: French New Wave Realism
genres.description: Existential youth wandering Parisian streets, breaking the fourth wall, utilizing jump cuts, conversational spontaneity, and breezy café banter.

genres.name: Italian Neorealism
genres.description: Working-class moral struggle set against raw bombed-out ruins, non-professional actors, natural light, and profound human dignity.

genres.name: Spaghetti Western
genres.description: Cynical antiheroes in dust-blown frontier towns, extreme wide desert vistas cutting to sweaty eye close-ups before lethal gun draws.

genres.name: German Expressionism
genres.description: Psychological madness projected onto external reality with jagged architectural angles, deep painted shadows, and theatrical physical distress.

genres.name: Korean New Wave Revenge Thriller
genres.description: Visceral morality tales driven by relentless physical retribution, dingy tiled hallways, blunt-force combat, and crushing emotional tragedy.

genres.name: Bollywood Masala Spectacle
genres.description: Multi-genre cinematic celebration blending dramatic romantic melodrama, larger-than-life hero entrances, explosive kinetic action, and grand emotional catharsis.

genres.name: Tollywood Mythic Hyper-Action
genres.description: Mythological superhuman heroism, physics-defying combat sequences, dramatic slow-motion dust impacts, and roaring crowd celebrations.

genres.name: Nordic Noir Procedural
genres.description: Brooding detectives investigating mysterious rural cases beneath desolate overcast skies, freezing coastal fjords, and atmospheric minimalist architecture.

genres.name: Latin American Magic Realism
genres.description: Everyday village life seamlessly intertwined with the supernatural, glowing ancestral spirits, impossible folklore, and vibrant tactile passions.

genres.name: Nollywood Urban Melodrama
genres.description: High-stakes familial power struggles, spiritual conflicts between tradition and mega-city modernity, flamboyant wealth, and intense emotional confrontations.

genres.name: Japanese Yakuza Honor Code
genres.description: Brutal clan betrayals inside tatami mat rooms, stoic code of duty (giri-ninjo), flashing katana blades, and blood-splattered raincoats.

genres.name: J-Horror Atmospheric Dread
genres.description: Creeping psychological terror born from technology and damp urban isolation, pale water-logged ghosts with black hair, and deafening silence.

genres.name: British Kitchen Sink Realism
genres.description: Gritty working-class industrial city life, factory smoke, cramped terraced brick housing, colloquial banter, and generational disillusionment.

genres.name: Classic American Film Noir
genres.description: Cynical private investigators, lethal femme fatales, venetian blind shadow slats, cigarette smoke haze, and corrupt rain-slicked midnight avenues.

genres.name: Tech-Noir & Cyber-Thriller
genres.description: Underground hackers and corporate enforcers navigating holographic billboards, wet pavement reflections, synthetic narcotics, and digital paranoia.

genres.name: Folk Horror Pagan Ritual
genres.description: Sun-drenched pastoral meadows concealing ancient agrarian cult rituals, pagan flower crowns, unsettling community silence, and sacrificial terror.

genres.name: Cosmic Horror & Eldritch Dread
genres.description: Scholars confronting incomprehensible geometries, sanity-eroding celestial voids, gelatinous non-Euclidean relics, and paralyzing human insignificance.

genres.name: Soviet Montage Epic
genres.description: Collision of dynamic intellectual imagery, rhythmic cutting, heroic collective worker gestures, monumental machinery, and stark angular framing.

genres.name: Action Genre
genres.description: Movies in theaction genreare defined by risk and stakes. While many movies may feature anaction sequence, to be appropriately categorized inside the action genre, the bulk of the content must be action-oriented, includingfight scenes,.

genres.name: Animation Genre
genres.description: Theanimationgenre is defined by inanimate objects being manipulated to appear as though they are living.

genres.name: Comedy Genre
genres.description: The comedy genreis defined by events that are intended to make someone laugh, no matter if the story is macabre, droll, or zany.

genres.name: Crime Genre
genres.description: The crime genre deals with both sides of the criminal justice system but does not focus on legislative matters or civil suits and legal actions.

genres.name: Drama Genre
genres.description: Thedramagenre is defined by conflict and often looks to reality rather than sensationalism.

genres.name: Experimental Genre
genres.description: Theexperimental genreis often defined by the idea that the work of art and entertainment does not fit into a particular genre or sub-genre, and is intended as such.

genres.name: Fantasy Genre
genres.description: The fantasy genre is defined by both circumstance and setting inside a fictional universe with an unrealistic set of natural laws.

genres.name: Historical Genre
genres.description: The historical genre can be split into two sections. One deals with accurate representations of historical accounts which can include biographies, autobiographies, and memoirs.

genres.name: Horror Genre
genres.description: Thehorror genreis centered upon depicting terrifying or macabre events for the sake of entertainment.

genres.name: Romance Genre
genres.description: The romance genre is defined by intimate relationships. Sometimes these movies can have a darker twist, but the idea is to lean on the naturalconflictderived from the pursuit of intimacy and love.

genres.name: Science Fiction Genre
genres.description: Science fiction moviesare defined by a mixture of speculation and science. While fantasy will explain through or make use of magic and mysticism, science fiction will use the changes and trajectory of technology and science.

genres.name: Thriller Genre
genres.description: A thriller story is mostly about the emotional purpose, which is to elicit strong emotions, mostly dealing with generating suspense and anxiety.

genres.name: Western Genre
genres.description: Westerns are defined by their setting and time period. The story needs to take place in the American West, which begins as far east as Missouri and extends to the Pacific ocean.

genres.name: Musical Genre
genres.description: Musicals originated as stage plays, but they soon became a favorite for manyfilm directorsand have even made their way into television.

genres.name: War Genre
genres.description: The war genre has a few debatable definitions, but we’re going to try to be as straightforward and impartial as humanly possible.

genres.name: Action film
genres.description: Film genre that predominantly features chase sequences, fights, shootouts, explosions, and stunt work.

genres.name: Adventure film
genres.description: The adventure film is a broad genre of film. Some early genre studies found it no different from the Western film or argued that adventure could encompass all Hollywood genres.

genres.name: Comedy film
genres.description: The comedy film is a film genre that emphasizes humor. These films are designed to amuse audiences and make them laugh.

genres.name: Coming-of-age story
genres.description: In genre studies, a coming-of-age story is a genre of literature, theatre, film, and video game that focuses on the growth of a protagonist from childhood to adulthood, or "coming of age".

genres.name: Crime film
genres.description: The crime film is a genre where the element of crime is key the films plot. Researchers of the genre, such as Nicole Hahn Rafter and Thomas Leitch noted the difficulty in defining the genre, saying it would be impractical to call every.

genres.name: Drama (film and television)
genres.description: Category or genre of narrative fiction (or semi-fiction) intended to be more serious than humorous in tone.

genres.name: Folk horror
genres.description: Subgenre of horror film and horror fiction that uses elements of folklore to invoke fear and foreboding.

genres.name: Gangster film
genres.description: A gangster film or gangster movie is a film belonging to a genre that focuses on gangs and organized crime.

genres.name: Heist film
genres.description: The heist film or caper film is a subgenre of crime films and the caper story, focused on the planning, execution, and aftermath of a significant robbery.

genres.name: Horror film
genres.description: Horror is a film genre that seeks to elicit physical or psychological fear in its viewers.

genres.name: Melodrama
genres.description: A melodrama is a dramatic work in which plot, typically sensationalized for a strong emotional appeal, takes precedence over detailed characterization.

genres.name: Psychological thriller
genres.description: Genre combining the thriller and psychological fiction genres. It is commonly used to describe literature or films that deal with psychological narratives in a thriller or thrilling setting.

genres.name: Romantic comedy
genres.description: Romantic comedy (commonly shortened to romcom or rom-com) is a sub-genre of comedy and romance fiction, focusing on lighthearted, humorous plot lines centered on romantic ideas, such as how love is able to surmount all obstacles.

genres.name: Screwball comedy
genres.description: Film subgenre of the romantic comedy genre that became popular during the Great Depression, beginning in the early 1930s and thriving until the early 1950s, that satirizes the traditional love story.

genres.name: Slapstick
genres.description: Style of humor involving exaggerated physical activity that exceeds the boundaries of normal physical comedy, which may involve both intentional violence and violence by mishap, often resulting from physical abuse or inept use of props.

genres.name: Supernatural horror film
genres.description: Genre that combines aspects of supernatural and horror film. Supernatural occurrences in such films often include ghosts and demons, and many supernatural horror films have elements of religion.

genres.name: Dark humor
genres.description: Dark humor, also known as black comedy, black humor, bleak comedy, dark comedy, gallows humor or morbid humor is a style of comedy that makes light of subject matter that is generally considered taboo, particularly subjects that are.

genres.name: Acid Western
genres.description: Subgenre of the Western film that emerged in the 1960s and 1970s that combines the metaphorical ambitions of critically acclaimed Westerns, such as Shane and The Searchers, with the excesses of the spaghetti Westerns.

genres.name: Biopunk
genres.description: Biopunk (a portmanteau of "biotechnology" or "biology" and "punk") is a subgenre of science fiction that focuses on biotechnology.

genres.name: Cyberpunk
genres.description: Subgenre of science fiction set in a dystopian future. It is characterized by its focus on a combination of "lowlife and high tech".

genres.name: Dark fantasy
genres.description: Dark fantasy or fantasy horror is a subgenre of literary, artistic, and cinematic fantasy works that incorporates elements of horror fiction.

genres.name: Dieselpunk
genres.description: Retrofuturistic subgenre of science fiction similar to steampunk or cyberpunk that combines the aesthetics of the diesel-based technology of the interwar period through to the 1950s with retro-futuristic technology and postmodern.

genres.name: Disaster film
genres.description: A disaster film or disaster movie is a film genre that has an impending or ongoing disaster as its subject and primary plot device.

genres.name: Documentary film
genres.description: A documentary film (often called simply a documentary) is a nonfiction motion picture intended to "document reality, primarily for instruction, education or maintaining a historical record".

genres.name: Fantasy film
genres.description: Fantasy films are films that belong to the fantasy genre with fantastic themes, usually magic, supernatural events, mythology, folklore, or exotic fantasy worlds.

genres.name: Martial arts film
genres.description: Martial arts films are a subgenre of action films that feature martial arts combat between characters.

genres.name: Mockumentary
genres.description: A mockumentary (a portmanteau of mock and documentary) is a type of film or television programme depicting fictional events, but presented as a documentary.

genres.name: Musical film
genres.description: Film genre in which songs by the characters are interwoven into the narrative, sometimes accompanied by dancing.

genres.name: Science fiction film
genres.description: Application of science fiction themes into a film genre. As such, it uses speculative, science-based depictions of phenomena that are not fully accepted by mainstream science, such as extraterrestrial lifeforms, spacecraft, robots,.

genres.name: Solarpunk
genres.description: Genre of speculative art and fiction which centers depictions of ecologically sustainable futures.

genres.name: Space opera
genres.description: Subgenre of science fiction and science fantasy that emphasizes epic outer space adventures set in a universe in which faster-than-light travel has become common.

genres.name: Steampunk
genres.description: Subgenre of science fiction that incorporates retro-futuristic technology and aesthetics prominently inspired by 19th-century industrial steam-powered machinery and design.

genres.name: War film
genres.description: Film genre concerned with warfare, typically about naval, air, or land battles, with combat scenes central to the drama.

genres.name: Western (genre)
genres.description: The Western is a genre of fiction typically set in the American frontier, commonly referred to as the “Old West” or “Wild West”.

genres.name: Wuxia
genres.description: Wuxia is a genre of Chinese fiction and low fantasy concerning the adventures of martial artists in ancient China.

genres.name: Apocalyptic and post-apocalyptic fiction
genres.description: Apocalyptic and post-apocalyptic fiction are subgenres of speculative fiction in which the Earth's (or another place's) civilization is collapsing or has collapsed.

genres.name: Action comedy
genres.description: Hybrid genre that combines elements of action fiction with comedy. While early action films feature stuntwork and humor, academic Cynthia King wrote that the genre only came into its own as a mainstay of the American action film genre.

genres.name: Animated documentary
genres.description: The animated documentary (also known as anidoc) is a moving image form that combines animation and documentary.

genres.name: Dystopia
genres.description: A dystopia (lit. "bad place") is an imagined world or society in which people lead wretched, dehumanized, fearful lives.

genres.name: Kaiju
genres.description: Kaiju (怪獣（かいじゅう）, kaijū; lit. 'strange beast') is a term used in film and media for a subgenre of monster films produced in Japan known as kaiju eiga (monster films), also serving as a subgenre of tokusatsu (special effects filmmaking).

genres.name: Road movie
genres.description: A road movie is a genre of film in which the main characters leave home on a road trip, typically altering the perspective from their everyday lives.

genres.name: Swashbuckler film
genres.description: A swashbuckler film is characterised by swordfighting and adventurous heroic characters, known as swashbucklers.

genres.name: Sword-and-sandal
genres.description: Sword-and-sandal, also known as peplum (pl.: pepla), is a subgenre of largely Italian-made historical, mythological, or biblical epic films mostly set in the Greco-Roman antiquity or the Middle Ages.

genres.name: Tokusatsu
genres.description: Tokusatsu (特撮（とくさつ）; lit. 'special filming') is a Japanese term for live-action films or television programs that make heavy use of practical special effects.

genres.name: B movie
genres.description: A B movie, or B film, is a type of low-budget commercial motion picture. Originally, during the Golden Age of Hollywood, this term specifically referred to films meant to be shown as the lesser-known second half of a double feature,.

genres.name: Found footage film
genres.description: Found footage is a cinematic technique and film genre in which all or a substantial part of the work is presented as if it were film or video recordings recorded by characters in the story, and later "found" and presented to the audience.

genres.name: Tech noir
genres.description: Hybrid genre of fiction, particularly film, combining film noir and science fiction, epitomized by Ridley Scott's Blade Runner (1982) and James Cameron's The Terminator (1984).

genres.name: Anthology film
genres.description: An anthology film (also known as an omnibus film, package film or portmanteau film) is a single film consisting of three or more shorter films, each complete in itself and distinguished from the other, though frequently tied together by.

genres.name: Art film
genres.description: An art film, arthouse film, or specialty film is an independent film aimed at a niche market rather than a mass market audience.

genres.name: Art horror
genres.description: Art horror or arthouse horror (sometimes called elevated horror) is a sub-genre of both horror films and art films.

genres.name: Arthouse animation
genres.description: Combination of art film and animated film.

genres.name: Arthouse science fiction film
genres.description: Arthouse science fiction (or arthouse sci-fi) is a combination of art and science fiction cinema.

genres.name: Bildungsroman
genres.description: In literary criticism, a bildungsroman is a literary genre that focuses on the psychological and moral growth and change of the protagonist from childhood to adulthood (coming of age).

genres.name: Biographical film
genres.description: A biographical film, or biopic (, biographical picture), is a film that dramatizes the life of a real person or sometimes a group of people.

genres.name: Buddy cop
genres.description: Film and television genre with plots involving two people of very different and conflicting personalities who are forced to work together to solve a crime or defeat criminals, often learning from each other in the process.

genres.name: Buddy film
genres.description: The buddy film is a subgenre of adventure and comedy film in which two people go on an adventure, mission, or road trip.

genres.name: Cartoon
genres.description: A cartoon is a type of visual art that is typically drawn, frequently animated, in an unrealistic or semi-realistic style.

genres.name: Chicano cinema
genres.description: Aspect of Mexican American cinema that refers to the filmmaking practices that emerged out of the cultural consciousness developed through the Chicano Movement.

genres.name: Children's film
genres.description: A children's film, or family film, is a film genre that generally relates to children in the context of home and family.

genres.name: 90s Fisheye Hip-Hop Video
genres.description: High-energy performance filmed with extreme 8mm fisheye lenses, glossy metallic windbreakers, vibrant yellow-orange backgrounds, and rapid low-angle camera rolls.

genres.name: Practical In-Camera Surrealism
genres.description: Clever practical optical illusions, choreographed human conveyor belts, cardboard city replicas, and continuous physical match-cuts without digital visual effects.

genres.name: High-Gloss Neon Trap Visualizer
genres.description: Late-night urban pursuit with luxury hyper-cars drifting on rain-soaked tarmac under saturated magenta and cyan rim-lighting and anamorphic streaks.

genres.name: Cyber-Y2K Industrial Rave
genres.description: Underground warehouse strobes, chrome futuristic eyewear, cybernetic fashion, rapid shutter-angle motion stutter, and relentless breakbeat pacing.

genres.name: Acoustic Indie Folk Single-Take
genres.description: Warm natural sunlight filtering through autumnal forest foliage as a lone musician performs an uninterrupted, gently drifting Steadicam ballad.

genres.name: High-Fashion Editorial Art Film
genres.description: Striking avant-garde silhouette poses, harsh on-camera flash against raw concrete walls, minimalist sound design, and hypnotic physical choreography.

genres.name: Lo-Fi VHS Bedroom Pop
genres.description: Dreamy hazy nostalgic video filmed on vintage analog camcorder, tracking static lines, pastel bedroom fairy lights, and intimate candid close-ups.

genres.name: Haute Parfumerie & Luxury Fragrance
genres.description: Ethereal slow-motion billowing silk, backlit golden sunbeams blooming through mist, statuesque models walking on water, and whispered French narration.

genres.name: Dynamic Automotive Mountain Pursuit
genres.description: High-performance sports car carving through winding alpine mountain passes at sunset, filmed from low-slung gyro-stabilized pursuit cranes.

genres.name: Minimalist Hardware & Tech Monolith
genres.description: Dark reflective obsidian environment, laser edge illumination highlighting brushed titanium and matte glass, precision turntable mechanical rotations.

genres.name: Phantom 1000fps Culinary Splash
genres.description: Microscopic liquid droplets colliding in ultra-slow motion, sizzling flames caramelizing sugar, flying fresh ingredients bursting through airborne water ribbons.

genres.name: High-Energy Kinetic Streetwear Campaign
genres.description: Aggressive speed-ramping, snap zooms, handheld running alongside athletes jumping across brutalist concrete steps in raw natural city light.

genres.name: Cinematic FPV Travel Adventure
genres.description: Seamless continuous FPV drone dive soaring through mountain ridges and dropping into a sunlit forest camp with pristine 4K color grading.

genres.name: Observational Cinema Verité
genres.description: Unobtrusive handheld camera documenting spontaneous human interactions in bustling open-air street markets with authentic ambient soundscapes.

genres.name: Guerrilla Investigative Dispatch
genres.description: Urgent low-light run-and-gun filming, direct microphone audio, harsh camera-mounted flashlight cutting through industrial ruins at 3 AM.

visual_styles.name: Stanley Kubrick Visual Grammar
visual_styles.description: Extreme one-point perspective symmetry, clinical emotional detachment, wide-angle spatial distortion, slow hypnotic tracking through monumental corridors.
visual_styles.key_motifs: One-point perspective, pristine white interiors, labyrinthine corridors, imposing symmetry, intense unblinking glares

visual_styles.name: David Lynch Surreal Dread
visual_styles.description: Dream-logic juxtaposition of 1950s wholesome Americana with nightmarish psychological decay, heavy red velvet curtains, flickering floor lamps, and deep industrial audio drone.
visual_styles.key_motifs: Red velvet drapery, chevron zigzag floors, flickering neon, mysterious smoky diners, uncanny doubles

visual_styles.name: Andrei Tarkovsky Poetic Transcendence
visual_styles.description: Monumental slow cinema tracking across waterlogged ruins, levitating figures, damp fertile earth, wind rippling through long grass, and deeply spiritual contemplation.
visual_styles.key_motifs: Water reflections, burning wooden houses, morning fog, damp earth, levitation, decaying classical paintings

visual_styles.name: Wong Kar-wai Melancholic Neon
visual_styles.description: Step-printed slow shutter motion blur, neon reflections on wet taxi windows, smoke swirling around lonely diners, and unrequited romantic longing in dense night markets.
visual_styles.key_motifs: Step-printing, 24fps motion trails, saturated neon green and amber, clock faces, cigarette smoke, cramped noodle stalls

visual_styles.name: Denis Villeneuve Monolithic Brutalism
visual_styles.description: Towering geometric architecture dominating tiny human figures, atmospheric dust and sand storms, muted monochromatic palettes, and thunderous low-frequency sonic presence.
visual_styles.key_motifs: Vast geometric monoliths, dust hazes, silhouettes against orange or grey skies, brutalist concrete, pristine symmetry

visual_styles.name: David Fincher Surgical Precision
visual_styles.description: Mechanical tripod pans perfectly synchronized with actor movement, desaturated yellow-green sickly color timing, low-key lighting, and relentless analytical scrutiny.
visual_styles.key_motifs: Desaturated sickly greens, low-key shadow contrast, computer-precise tracking moves, subterranean filing rooms, heavy rain

visual_styles.name: Wes Anderson Symmetrical Whimsy
visual_styles.description: Strict planar symmetry, candy-colored pastel color palettes, rapid 90-degree whip pans, miniature diorama staging, and meticulous vintage typography.
visual_styles.key_motifs: Planar symmetry, pastel pink and mustard yellow, retro luggage, binoculars, antique typography, cross-section sets

visual_styles.name: Akira Kurosawa Dynamic Composition
visual_styles.description: Weather elements as dramatic forces (deluges of torrential rain, howling dust winds), dynamic triangle character blocking, and long-lens depth compression.
visual_styles.key_motifs: Torrential rainstorms, blowing dust, triangle group compositions, samurai topknots, fluttering banners, horizontal tracking

visual_styles.name: Guillermo del Toro Clockwork Fairy Tale
visual_styles.description: Painterly amber and teal contrast, tactile mechanical clockwork apparatus, grotesque yet empathetic biological monsters, and gothic subterranean labyrinths.
visual_styles.key_motifs: Amber and cyan lighting, brass gears, biological prosthetics, subterranean arches, gothic stained glass, formalin jars

visual_styles.name: Hayao Miyazaki Soaring Pastoral
visual_styles.description: Breathtaking hand-painted cumulus clouds, soaring flight sequences, lush pastoral European hillsides, cozy domestic warmth, and environmental reverence.
visual_styles.key_motifs: Towering summer clouds, hand-crafted aircraft, lush meadow grass, sparkling water springs, glowing lanterns

visual_styles.name: Gaspar Noé Hallucinogenic Immersion
visual_styles.description: Floating Steadicam ceiling perspectives drifting through doorways, pulsing strobe lights, disorienting 360-degree rolls, and sensory neon euphoria.
visual_styles.key_motifs: Pulsing red and amber strobe lights, overhead ceiling tracking, spinning camera axes, nightclub delirium, neon signs

visual_styles.name: Nicolas Winding Refn Hyper-Stylized Neon
visual_styles.description: Static, operatic compositions drenched in saturated magenta and electric cyan neon, stoic psychopathic protagonists, long pregnant silences, and brutal eruptive violence.
visual_styles.key_motifs: Saturated neon magenta, deep ink shadows, luxury automotive interiors, silent stoic stares, blood on polished tiles

visual_styles.name: Terry Gilliam Baroque Absurdity
visual_styles.description: Extreme wide-angle Dutch tilts, labyrinthine bureaucratic ductwork, retro-futuristic clunky cathode screens, and frantic surrealist physical comedy.
visual_styles.key_motifs: Dutch angles, 14mm wide-angle distortion, pneumatic tubes, towering paper stacks, rusted clockwork, eccentric costumes

visual_styles.name: Claire Denis Tactile Sensuality
visual_styles.description: Extreme macro close-ups of sweating skin, rhythmic physical choreography, sun-bleached desert dust, elliptical editing, and unspoken colonial and psychological tension.
visual_styles.key_motifs: Macro skin textures, desert mirages, sun-bleached salt flats, repetitive military drills, silent glances

visual_styles.name: Terrence Malick Golden-Hour Transcendence
visual_styles.description: Wide-angle roving Steadicam tracking behind characters through tall grass, low-angle natural golden hour backlighting, whispery poetic voiceovers, and cosmic imagery.
visual_styles.key_motifs: Golden hour lens flares, wind through tall wheat, wide-angle upward tilt, flowing water streams, soaring sunbeams

visual_styles.name: Park Chan-wook Baroque Revenge
visual_styles.description: Elaborate geometric wallpaper patterns, ingenious match cuts across time and space, dark macabre wit, and operatic emotional crescendos.
visual_styles.key_motifs: Repetitive wallpaper patterns, symmetrical corridor tracking, green tile bathrooms, elaborate seafood, leather-bound diaries

visual_styles.name: George Miller Kinetic High-Octane
visual_styles.description: Center-framed hyper-kinetic action choreography, speed-ramped vehicular mayhem, high-contrast saturated desert orange and cobalt sky, and practical stunt madness.
visual_styles.key_motifs: Center-framed action, post-apocalyptic custom vehicles, roaring exhaust flames, desert dust clouds, chrome skulls

visual_styles.name: Brutalist architecture
visual_styles.description: Architectural style that emerged during the 1950s in the United Kingdom, among the reconstruction projects of the post-war era.

visual_styles.name: Constructivism (art)
visual_styles.description: Constructivism (Russian: конструктивизм, romanized: konstruktivizm) is an early twentieth-century art movement founded in 1915 by Vladimir Tatlin and Alexander Rodchenko.

visual_styles.name: Cubism
visual_styles.description: Early-20th-century avant-garde art movement which began in Paris. It revolutionized painting and the visual arts, and sparked artistic innovations in music, ballet, literature, and architecture.

visual_styles.name: Dada
visual_styles.description: Dada or Dadaism was an international art movement that developed in the context of World War I, its aftermath, and the Futurist movement.

visual_styles.name: De Stijl
visual_styles.description: De Stijl was a Dutch art movement founded in 1917 by a group of artists and architects based in Leiden (Theo van Doesburg, J.

visual_styles.name: Fauvism
visual_styles.description: Fauvism ( FOH-viz-əm) is a style of painting and an art movement that emerged in France at the beginning of the 20th century.

visual_styles.name: Futurism
visual_styles.description: Futurism was an artistic and social movement that originated in Italy, and to a lesser extent in other countries, in the early 20th century.

visual_styles.name: Gothic art
visual_styles.description: Style of medieval art that developed in Northern France out of Romanesque art in the 12th century, led by the concurrent development of Gothic architecture.

visual_styles.name: Kitsch
visual_styles.description: Kitsch ( KITCH; loanword from German) is a term applied to art and design that is perceived as naïve imitation, overly eccentric, gratuitous, or of banal taste.

visual_styles.name: Minimalism
visual_styles.description: Art movement that emphasizes reducing art to its essentials, focusing on the object itself and the viewer's experience, with as little mediation from the artist as possible.

visual_styles.name: Op art
visual_styles.description: Op art, short for optical art, is a style of visual art that uses distorted or manipulated geometrical patterns, often to create optical illusions.

visual_styles.name: Pop art
visual_styles.description: Art movement that emerged in the United Kingdom and the United States during the mid-to-late 1950s.

visual_styles.name: Precisionism
visual_styles.description: Modernist art movement that emerged in the United States after World War I. Influenced by Cubism, Purism, and Futurism, Precisionist artists reduced subjects to their essential geometric shapes, eliminated detail, and often used planes.

visual_styles.name: Romanticism
visual_styles.description: Romanticism (also known as the Romantic movement or Romantic era) was an artistic and intellectual movement that originated in Europe towards the end of the 18th century.

visual_styles.name: Suprematism
visual_styles.description: Suprematism (Russian: супремати́зм) is an early 20th-century art movement focused on the fundamentals of geometry (circles, squares, rectangles), painted in a limited range of colors.

visual_styles.name: Surrealism
visual_styles.description: Art and cultural movement that developed in Europe in the aftermath of World War I in which artists aimed to allow the unconscious mind to express itself, often resulting in the depiction of illogical or dreamlike scenes and ideas.

visual_styles.name: Abstract art
visual_styles.description: Abstract art uses visual language of shape, form, color, and line to create a composition which may exist with a degree of independence from visual references in the world.

visual_styles.name: Abstract expressionism
visual_styles.description: Abstract expressionism in the United States emerged as a distinct art movement in the aftermath of World War II and gained mainstream acceptance in the 1950s, a shift from the American social realism of the 1930s influenced by the Great.

visual_styles.name: Abstract impressionism
visual_styles.description: Art movement that originated in New York City, in the 1940s. It involves the painting of a subject such as real-life scenes, objects, or people (portraits) in an Impressionist style, but with an emphasis on varying measures of abstraction.

visual_styles.name: Academic art
visual_styles.description: Academic art, academicism, or academism, is a style of painting and sculpture produced under the influence of European academies of art.

visual_styles.name: Conceptual art

visual_styles.name: 2 Tone

visual_styles.name: Clockpunk

visual_styles.name: Cyberprep

visual_styles.name: Hauntology

visual_styles.name: Rococo

visual_styles.name: Sovietwave

visual_styles.name: Utopian Scholastic

visual_styles.name: 8-Bit

visual_styles.name: 80s-90s Afrocentrism

visual_styles.name: 80s Workout

visual_styles.name: 90s Cool

visual_styles.key_motifs: Outback scenes, Animals (Native and Invasive), Distorted Land, Ghosts, History and myth.

visual_styles.key_motifs: Australian wildlife, koalas, kangaroos, and galahs, native flora and fauna, Aboriginal art, low-set cream brick homes, Queenslanders, nostalgic kitsch, retro design elements, fairy bread

visual_styles.name: Autumn Aesthetic

visual_styles.key_motifs: Pumpkin spice lattes, chunky knit sweaters, falling leaves, cozy blankets, candles, classic books, pumpkin patches, apple cider

visual_styles.name: Avant Apocalypse

visual_styles.key_motifs: Deconstruction, asymmetry, layering, neutral tones, cut-outs, unconventional silhouettes

camera_movements.name: Slow Forward Dolly Push-In
camera_movements.description: Camera moves physically forward on smooth tracks toward the subject at a steady deliberate pace, amplifying dramatic intimacy and psychological focus.

camera_movements.name: Slow Dolly Pull-Back & Reveal
camera_movements.description: Camera tracks slowly backward from a tight focal point through doorways or obstacles, gradually revealing monumental scale or hidden surrounding context.

camera_movements.name: Lateral Tracking / Trucking Shot
camera_movements.description: Camera travels horizontally parallel to walking or running subjects, gliding past foreground environmental pillars to create pronounced parallax depth.

camera_movements.name: Dynamic Steadicam Glide
camera_movements.description: Stabilized body-mounted camera floats effortlessly at eye level through intricate architectural corridors, pivoting smoothly around moving actors.

camera_movements.name: FPV Acrobatic Drone Dive
camera_movements.description: High-velocity agile quadcopter dives vertically down building facades, banks sharply around corners, and skims inches above ground level with visceral speed.

camera_movements.name: Techno-Jib Vertical Swoop
camera_movements.description: Mechanical telescoping crane arm swoops vertically from an extreme close-up of hands or eyes up to a sweeping 50-foot bird's-eye panoramic vista.

camera_movements.name: Snorricam Body-Mounted Rig
camera_movements.description: Camera physically clamped to the actor's torso; the subject's face remains locked dead center in frame while the surrounding world spins and pitches violently.

camera_movements.name: High-Speed Whip Pan / Swish Cut
camera_movements.description: Violent, rapid horizontal rotational flick causing intense motion blur, instantly snapping attention to a surprise subject or serving as an invisible transition.

camera_movements.name: Crash Zoom / Snap Zoom
camera_movements.description: Ultra-fast manual lens zoom snapping from an extreme wide perspective directly into the actor's startled eyes within a fraction of a second.

camera_movements.name: Vertigo Effect (Zolly / Dolly Zoom)
camera_movements.description: Camera physically dollies forward while simultaneously zooming out the lens, keeping the subject identical in size while background space warps and expands.

camera_movements.name: 360-Degree Continuous Circular Orbit
camera_movements.description: Camera glides along a complete 360-degree circular perimeter around subjects frozen or moving in slow motion, celebrating sculptural spatial geometry.

camera_movements.name: Bolt Robotic High-Speed Motion Control
camera_movements.description: High-speed industrial robotic arm maneuvers the camera along mathematically exact coordinates in milliseconds, executing flawless geometric match-cuts.

camera_movements.name: Organic Handheld Cinema Verité
camera_movements.description: Shoulder-mounted camera with natural human micro-jitter and breathing movements, instinctively reframing action with urgent documentary realism.

camera_movements.name: Overhead God's-Eye Top-Down View
camera_movements.description: Camera positioned strictly perpendicular to the ground pointing 90 degrees downward, turning human choreography and architecture into flat geometric abstractions.

camera_movements.name: Low-Angle Dutch Tilt / Canted Frame
camera_movements.description: Camera tilted steeply upward from ankle height with a 25-degree diagonal roll on the horizon, imbuing subjects with menacing authority or psychic distress.

camera_movements.name: Laowa Tubular Probe Lens Fly-Through
camera_movements.description: Slender waterproof tubular probe lens with built-in LED ring sliding through microscopic openings, between foliage, and inside liquid droplets.

camera_movements.name: Locked-Off Studio Tableau
camera_movements.description: Completely motionless heavy studio tripod with zero camera roll, tilt, or pan, allowing subtle character blocking and wind motion to animate the frame.

camera_movements.name: Step-Printing Shutter Motion Blur
camera_movements.description: Filmed at low frame rates with high shutter angle and digitally repeated frames, causing kinetic action to leave glowing, ethereal motion trails.

camera_movements.name: First-Person POV Helmet Mount
camera_movements.description: Direct subjective eye-level viewpoint with the character's arms entering peripheral vision, immersing the viewer directly into their immediate sensory crisis.

camera_movements.name: Russian Arm Roof-Mounted Pursuit Crane
camera_movements.description: High-speed pursuit vehicle equipped with a gyro-stabilized roof crane skimming inches above tarmac alongside racing cars through high-speed turns.

camera_movements.name: Aerial
camera_movements.description: Footage captured from aircraft or airborne platforms like drones, creating expansive elevated perspectives of landscapes and scenes.

camera_movements.name: Altered state
camera_movements.description: An effect simulating altered perception from drugs or alcohol through distorted visuals, vibrant colors, surreal imagery, rapid editing, and kaleidoscopic patterns.

camera_movements.name: Animation
camera_movements.description: Cel animation uses hand-drawn frames on transparent sheets, inked, painted, and layered to create traditional animated sequences.

camera_movements.name: Anthropo
camera_movements.description: Anthropomorphism gives human characteristics to animals or inanimate objects, making them behave, communicate, and express emotions like people do.

camera_movements.name: Arc
camera_movements.description: The arc movement shot smoothly rotates a camera in a circular motion around a subject, creating an elegant, sophisticated effect that enhances visual storytelling.

camera_movements.name: Architexture
camera_movements.description: Using animation textures to make buildings, cities, and architectural structures appear to move and shift dynamically.

camera_movements.name: Bolt Cam
camera_movements.description: An incredibly rapid motorized camera arm that moves up to 6 feet per second in any direction, creating dynamic, fast-moving shots.

camera_movements.name: Boomerang
camera_movements.description: A video clip that plays forward then reverses, making subjects repeat actions in a seamless continuous loop resembling a boomerang's motion.

camera_movements.name: Bullet Time
camera_movements.description: Bullet time freezes action by capturing scenes from multiple camera angles simultaneously, creating the illusion of slowed motion while the camera moves dynamically around the stationary scene.

camera_movements.name: Camera Roll
camera_movements.description: The entire scene rotates, typically 180 degrees, creating a dynamic spinning effect that reorients the viewer's perspective of the composition.

camera_movements.name: Central Framing
camera_movements.description: Centering the subject in film framing emphasizes symmetry, drawing attention to convey visual impact and significance in a shot.

camera_movements.name: Choreo
camera_movements.description: Choreographed dance movements integrated with visuals and music to enhance storytelling, evoke emotion, and symbolize thematic elements through body language and rhythm.

camera_movements.name: Cinemagraph
camera_movements.description: A still photograph with subtle, repeating motion in one or a few elements, creating a seamless loop between static and dynamic imagery.

camera_movements.name: Close-Up
camera_movements.description: Close-Up fills the screen with part of a subject, such as a person's head or face, allowing emotions and character reactions to dominate the scene.

camera_movements.name: Collage
camera_movements.description: The collage technique combines multiple images and video clips into a single composition, creating a visually eclectic and layered narrative.

camera_movements.name: Color Shift
camera_movements.description: A scene's colors shift dramatically for visual effect, creating mood changes or emphasizing narrative moments through chromatic transformation.

camera_movements.name: Conveyor
camera_movements.description: A visual transition where scenes move sequentially across the frame like objects on a conveyor belt, creating a flowing movement between distinct shots or settings.

camera_movements.name: Crash cut
camera_movements.description: A rapid zoom into a scene that abruptly cuts to another scene, creating a dynamic transition between shots.

camera_movements.name: Cut-ins
camera_movements.description: A cinematic transition where the shot zooms into a closer element of the same scene, creating an intensified focus on specific details within the frame.

camera_movements.name: Datamosh
camera_movements.description: Datamoshing creates glitchy, psychedelic visual distortions by corrupting video data, producing fragmented, pixelated effects resembling a blender-like digital breakdown.

camera_movements.name: Diorama
camera_movements.description: A technique creating scenes using three-dimensional miniature or full-sized models, often enclosed in glass, to produce detailed replica environments for filming.

camera_movements.name: Distortions
camera_movements.description: Distortions are visual effects that warp, bend, or twist the image through lens aberrations, digital manipulation, or in-camera techniques to create surreal or dreamlike visual aesthetics.

camera_movements.name: Dolly
camera_movements.description: A camera technique where the lens physically moves closer to a subject along a track or via handheld/stabilized equipment, drawing attention to specific details or character emotions.

camera_movements.name: Dolly Zoom
camera_movements.description: A camera technique that simultaneously moves toward a subject while adjusting the lens focal length away, creating a disorienting effect that distorts spatial perception and emphasizes psychological moments.

camera_movements.name: Double Dolly
camera_movements.description: A camera technique combining dolly zoom with simultaneous subject and camera movement, creating dynamic visual distortion while the scene moves forward.

camera_movements.name: Double Exposure
camera_movements.description: Layering multiple images on top of each other to create surreal, dreamlike visual effects that blend subjects together for artistic or stylistic impact.

camera_movements.name: Dreamcore
camera_movements.description: Dreamcore is a surrealist visual style using dream and nightmare motifs to create nostalgic, eerie imagery with disorienting spaces and uncanny atmospheres.

camera_movements.name: Duplication
camera_movements.description: The cloning technique creates multiple versions of the same actor or object within a single frame or sequence, achieving an illusion of duplication through in-camera or post-production methods.

camera_movements.name: Dutch Angle
camera_movements.description: The camera tilts diagonally to create visual disorientation, conveying unease, tension, instability or chaos to heighten emotional impact.

camera_movements.name: Dystopian
camera_movements.description: Dystopian visual style showcases dehumanizing, oppressive futures through dark aesthetics, highlighting themes of totalitarianism, environmental collapse, and human resilience against adversity.

camera_movements.name: Echo print
camera_movements.description: A motion blur effect that leaves trailing frames behind the main action before catching up, creating a ghosting or accordion-like visual effect reminiscent of step-printing.

camera_movements.name: Epiphany
camera_movements.description: A sudden moment of realization captured visually, often showing a character's facial expression or reaction when they understand something important or have a breakthrough.

camera_movements.name: Falling
camera_movements.description: A cinematic technique capturing subjects dropping through space, often used in music videos and film to convey weightlessness, disorientation, or surreal dreamlike sequences.

camera_movements.name: Fast Motion
camera_movements.description: Filming at a lower frame rate than normal playback speed, so action appears sped up when played back at normal speed, creating a comedic or urgent, time-condensing visual effect.

camera_movements.name: Feedback
camera_movements.description: Visual distortions mimicking analog TV glitches, characterized by fragmented, pixelated, or distorted elements common in 90s-2000s broadcast interference.

camera_movements.name: First-Person
camera_movements.description: The camera becomes the character, showing the world as if through their own eyes, creating an immersive perspective where viewers see what the character sees.

camera_movements.name: Fisheye
camera_movements.description: A wide-angle lens technique creating distorted, circular perspective with bulging edges, used to add surreal immersion or emphasize claustrophobia and tension in scenes.

camera_movements.name: Fixed Cam
camera_movements.description: Camera remains stationary while the subject stays constant in frame; background elements shift and change around the fixed subject.

camera_movements.name: Flash Cut
camera_movements.description: Rapidly flashing a series of images in quick succession to create a disorienting or hypnotic visual effect, often used as a type of accelerated match cut.

camera_movements.name: Floating UI
camera_movements.description: Digital interface elements appear on-screen in abstract, layered ways to help convey information or technology within the frame.

camera_movements.name: Focal shift
camera_movements.description: A cinematographic technique where the camera's focus transitions between different points of interest, shifting attention from one character or object to another within the same shot.

camera_movements.name: Fourth Wall
camera_movements.description: Characters acknowledge and address the viewer directly through the lens, breaking narrative illusion to create audience connection or comment on storytelling conventions.

camera_movements.name: FPV Drone
camera_movements.description: An immersive aerial perspective captured by a drone camera that simulates the pilot's first-person view, creating dynamic, fast-moving footage through environments.

camera_movements.name: Freeze Frame
camera_movements.description: A single frame of film is repeated to create a frozen, still image effect on screen, often used to punctuate a dramatic or comedic beat.

camera_movements.name: Generative
camera_movements.description: Artificial intelligence generates visual content based on text prompts by learning patterns from training data, producing new visuals with similar characteristics.

camera_movements.name: Gesture
camera_movements.description: Actors simulate touching, swiping, and scrolling motions as if interacting with invisible phone screens or digital interfaces in the physical world.

camera_movements.name: Ground Level
camera_movements.description: Camera positioned approximately 1-2 feet above ground level, capturing scenes from a child's or animal's perspective without looking directly upward.

camera_movements.name: Halation
camera_movements.description: Light scattering within film emulsion creates a diffuse halo or glow around bright areas through reflection off the film base.

camera_movements.name: Handheld
camera_movements.description: A camera technique using handheld or apparent handheld footage, creating shaky, unsteady motion to convey documentary, news-gathering, or ad hoc cinematic feel.

camera_movements.name: Hard Light
camera_movements.description: Hard light is a cinematic technique using sharp, directional lighting with high contrast to create dramatic shadows and defined light patterns on subjects.

camera_movements.name: Haze
camera_movements.description: Soft photography technique using out-of-focus and hazy effects to create dreamy, nostalgic visuals with blurred details and soft color palettes.

camera_movements.name: High Angle
camera_movements.description: A camera shot positioned above the subject, angled downward to create vulnerability or weakness, distinct from overhead shots by its angular rather than straight-down view.

camera_movements.name: Infinite Loop
camera_movements.description: A seamless looping visual that creates the illusion of continuous, endless motion or action without apparent beginning or end.

camera_movements.name: Interview
camera_movements.description: The capture of a person responding to questions posed by an off-screen interviewer, typically used in news and documentary formats.

camera_movements.name: Jump cut
camera_movements.description: A transition showing the same subject appearing to jump forward in time between two shots of identical framing and composition.

camera_movements.name: Kaleidoscope
camera_movements.description: A visual technique using optical devices or digital mirroring to create symmetrical, repeating patterns that transform footage into kaleidoscopic imagery.

camera_movements.name: Lazy Susan
camera_movements.description: The camera remains centered while panning left or right to different actors or objects, mimicking rotation on a lazy susan turntable.

camera_movements.name: Levitation
camera_movements.description: Where a character or object appears to float or hover in air without visible support, creating magic, supernatural, or futuristic effects.

camera_movements.name: Light Flash
camera_movements.description: A sudden, bright flash of light that momentarily illuminates or obscures the scene, creating a dramatic visual punctuation or transition effect.

camera_movements.name: Locked-On
camera_movements.description: The camera locks onto and follows a specific subject, keeping it centered while the background moves around it.

camera_movements.name: Low Angle
camera_movements.description: A low-angle shot positions the camera below eye level looking upward, making subjects appear towering, powerful, and dominant while creating an imposing perspective.

camera_movements.name: Magical realism
camera_movements.description: Magical elements seamlessly integrated into realistic, mundane environments where characters treat the extraordinary as ordinary.

camera_movements.name: Magnification
camera_movements.description: A cinematic technique creating a macro close-up shot viewed through a magnifying-glass frame within the larger scene.

camera_movements.name: Masking
camera_movements.description: Creating masks to isolate specific frame areas, enabling precise control over integrating visual effects, CGI elements, or different footage seamlessly.

camera_movements.name: Match Cut
camera_movements.description: A match cut seamlessly links two entirely different scenes by connecting similar visual elements, creating an unexpected transition that shifts narrative context while maintaining visual continuity.

camera_movements.name: Match motion
camera_movements.description: When a camera's motion seamlessly continues across a cut, making the movement flow uninterrupted from one shot to the next.

camera_movements.name: Match Split
camera_movements.description: A split-screen technique where the division creates a unified, seamless image across the frame rather than appearing as separate shots.

camera_movements.name: Maximalism
camera_movements.description: A visual style featuring excess through bold colors, patterns, textures, and layers that challenges viewers' perception of the medium's artificiality.

camera_movements.name: Mixed Media
camera_movements.description: Mixed Media blends multiple visual mediums, such as live-action footage, animation, photography, and digital art, into cohesive compositions within a single frame.

camera_movements.name: Morphing
camera_movements.description: Morphing is a special effect technique that transforms one image or object into another using computer-generated animation to show character or object evolution.

camera_movements.name: Motion Blur
camera_movements.description: Motion blur is a cinematic technique where moving subjects appear streaked or blurred, creating a sense of speed and dynamic motion.

camera_movements.name: Night Vision
camera_movements.description: Low-light filming using infrared sensors or light amplification technology to capture visible footage in darkness or surveillance conditions.

camera_movements.name: Object Portal
camera_movements.description: An object serves as a visual gateway, transporting viewers from one scene or world to another through a seamless transition.

camera_movements.name: Object POV
camera_movements.description: The camera takes the perspective of an inanimate object, with characters looking directly at it as if viewing a mirror or screen rather than breaking the fourth wall.

camera_movements.name: Omnidirectional
camera_movements.description: A 360-degree camera captures everything around a sphere, creating immersive shots that can be compressed into a ball or stretched across the screen.

camera_movements.name: Overhead
camera_movements.description: An overhead shot positions the camera directly above a subject, shooting downward to create a detached, bird's-eye perspective that conveys distance or divine observation.

camera_movements.name: Over the Shoulder
camera_movements.description: Camera positioned behind one character facing another, showing the first character's shoulder and back of head while viewing the second character's face.

camera_movements.name: Pan
camera_movements.description: A stationary camera rotates horizontally to follow action, making the scene appear to move while the camera stays fixed in place.

camera_movements.name: Parallax
camera_movements.description: Foreground and background elements move at different speeds to create depth illusion and visual layering effects.

camera_movements.name: Pass Through
camera_movements.description: The camera or lens physically passes through an object or person in the frame, often achieved with FPV drones in wide shots or probe lenses in close-ups.

camera_movements.name: Pedestal
camera_movements.description: A camera movement where the tripod stays fixed while the camera moves vertically upward or downward, creating an illusion of rising or falling relative to the subject.

camera_movements.name: Photogrammetry
camera_movements.description: 3D modeling technique using multiple 2D images to reconstruct objects or scenes, creating realistic three-dimensional models for mapping, surveying, and virtual environments.

camera_movements.name: Pixel Art
camera_movements.description: Pixel art animation uses hand-drawn pixels frame-by-frame to create retro-styled digital animations, or live-action footage pixelated for stylistic effect.

camera_movements.name: Probe
camera_movements.description: A specialized narrow probe lens enabling extreme close-ups and macro photography, creating visually striking detailed perspectives in tight or hard-to-reach spaces.

camera_movements.name: Product
camera_movements.description: Videography that prominently features and showcases a product, often highlighting its distinctive features and design elements.

camera_movements.name: Profile
camera_movements.description: Camera positioned to show the subject's side profile, highlighting facial features or creating distance and detachment, commonly used in dialogue and reaction shots.

camera_movements.name: Projections
camera_movements.description: Using projectors to display images, videos, or graphics onto surfaces like walls, buildings, or screens within the scene.

camera_movements.name: Quick Cuts
camera_movements.description: Rapid-fire cutting between multiple shots in quick succession, creating a frenetic, energetic visual rhythm commonly associated with filmmaker Edgar Wright's style.

camera_movements.name: Ratio Switch
camera_movements.description: Intentionally changing image dimensions on screen through zooming, cropping, or adding black bars to shift perspective, emphasize elements, or enhance immersion.

camera_movements.name: Reflections
camera_movements.description: Capturing subjects through mirrors or windows, creating layered visual compositions where reflected and direct imagery coexist within the frame.

camera_movements.name: Scale Shift
camera_movements.description: Using forced perspective to create illusions of scale, making small objects appear gigantic or large subjects look miniature.

camera_movements.name: Screen in Screen
camera_movements.description: A screen or frame displayed within the main shot, showing content inside the composition while maintaining the outer framing intact.

camera_movements.name: Set Transition
camera_movements.description: A set transforms into another form through practical effects, such as walls falling away or entire sets lifting up to reveal new environments.

camera_movements.name: Shadow Box
camera_movements.description: Framing visuals within the available space without filling the entire frame, leaving negative space around the subject or action.

camera_movements.name: Shallow Focus
camera_movements.description: Using shallow depth of field to selectively focus on subjects while blurring backgrounds, drawing viewer attention to specific characters or objects within the frame.

camera_movements.name: Silhouette
camera_movements.description: A striking cinematic shot where the subject appears as a dark, featureless silhouette against a brighter background, emphasizing shape and form over facial details.

camera_movements.name: Slit-scan
camera_movements.description: A visual effect that distorts images by scanning a narrow vertical or horizontal slit across scenes, creating surreal, abstract visuals that convey movement and time passage.

camera_movements.name: Slow Motion
camera_movements.description: Slow motion captures action at high frame rates, then plays it back at normal speed to create a stretched-out, detailed view of rapid movement.

camera_movements.name: Snorricam
camera_movements.description: A body-mounted rig fixes the camera to an actor's torso, keeping their face locked in frame while the background sways and shifts around them.

camera_movements.name: Speed Ramp
camera_movements.description: A shift in speed within a single shot, transitioning between slow motion, standard speed, and fast motion for dynamic visual impact.

camera_movements.name: Split Diopter
camera_movements.description: A lens attachment that maintains sharp focus on two objects at different distances simultaneously, used to create visual emphasis and narrative connection between foreground and background elements.

camera_movements.name: Split Screen
camera_movements.description: Dividing the frame into multiple simultaneous segments, each showing different action, creating dramatic visual intensity across distinct areas.

camera_movements.name: Step-print
camera_movements.description: Step-printing repeats individual film frames multiple times to create slow-motion or stuttering visual effects by reducing the perceived frame rate.

camera_movements.name: Stop Motion
camera_movements.description: Stop motion is a filmmaking technique where objects are physically repositioned in small increments between individual photograph frames, creating the illusion of independent movement when the sequence plays back.

camera_movements.name: Stutter
camera_movements.description: Frames are repeated, skipped, or manipulated to create choppy, jittery motion that emphasizes movement, disorientation, or adds energy to scenes.

camera_movements.name: Stylistic Suck
camera_movements.description: Intentionally employing a deliberately poor or cheesy aesthetic to create irony and humor by embracing the absurdity of a particular genre.

camera_movements.name: Tableau
camera_movements.description: A carefully arranged and aesthetically pleasing composition resembling a painting, where cinematographers create picturesque, visually striking scenes through deliberate framing and positioning.

camera_movements.name: Thermal
camera_movements.description: Mimics thermal-imaging cameras by displaying heat signatures and temperature variations in a scene, creating a distinctive dramatic look through infrared-style color mapping.

camera_movements.name: Tilt
camera_movements.description: A cinematographic technique where the camera moves vertically up or down from a fixed position, mimicking the natural motion of tilting one's head.

camera_movements.name: Tilt Shift
camera_movements.description: Tilt Shift uses specialized lenses to create an optical illusion making real scenes appear like miniature toy models through selective focus and depth manipulation.

camera_movements.name: Tracking
camera_movements.description: The camera follows a subject in motion, often used for dialogue scenes or character introductions to maintain continuous, dynamic framing.

camera_movements.name: Transformation
camera_movements.description: A character or object visually morphs into something entirely different, creating a seamless metamorphosis effect between two distinct forms.

camera_movements.name: Transitions
camera_movements.description: How one shot or scene changes to the next, guiding viewers between points and creating emotional effects through various editing methods.

camera_movements.name: Trucking
camera_movements.description: The camera moves laterally alongside the subject, creating dynamic energy and following action like car chases or characters moving through a scene.

camera_movements.name: Two Shot
camera_movements.description: A two shot frames two people in the same shot, with subjects positioned at varying distances from the camera rather than necessarily adjacent to one another.

camera_movements.name: Typography
camera_movements.description: Typography in film uses fonts, letterforms, and textual elements to enhance storytelling, establish mood, convey information, and evoke emotion throughout the visual narrative.

camera_movements.name: Ultra Wide
camera_movements.description: A cinematography technique using extremely wide-angle lenses or perspectives that capture expansive horizontal scenes with minimal depth distortion, creating panoramic framing.

camera_movements.name: Underwater
camera_movements.description: Any shot filmed submerged in water, capturing scenes with the specific visual characteristics of aquatic environments.

camera_movements.name: Video Game
camera_movements.description: Any shot created within a video-game aesthetic, mimicking the graphics, HUD elements, or camera behavior of interactive game footage.

camera_movements.name: Video Portraits
camera_movements.description: A short-form video portrait captures a person or group, reflecting their character and background, often used in documentaries and promotional content to convey personality.

camera_movements.name: Vignette
camera_movements.description: A darkening effect around the edges of the frame that draws viewer attention toward the center, commonly used for dramatic focus.

camera_movements.name: Vintage
camera_movements.description: A film technique presenting images as discovered archival or old footage, achieved through naturalistic cinematography, handheld camera work, and raw, degraded visual aesthetics.

camera_movements.name: Void
camera_movements.description: A dream-like minimalist space devoid of visual elements, creating an intentionally empty aesthetic that emphasizes absence and simplicity.

camera_movements.name: Voyeur
camera_movements.description: The voyeur technique captures subjects unaware they're being observed, creating an intrusive perspective that reveals private moments as if secretly watching through windows or from hidden vantage points.

camera_movements.name: Wandering
camera_movements.description: The camera moves through an environment as if the viewer is walking through it, creating an immersive first-person perspective of the scene.

camera_movements.name: Weirdcore
camera_movements.description: A surrealist visual style using amateur or low-quality imagery edited to evoke confusion, disorientation, dread, and nostalgia through deliberately unsettling compositions.

camera_movements.name: Whip Pan
camera_movements.description: The camera rapidly pans left or right, creating motion-blur streaks that make the transition between two scenes appear continuous and energetic.

camera_movements.name: Wide shot
camera_movements.description: A camera framing technique that captures expansive scenes from a distance, showing the full environment and context while keeping subjects small within the frame.

camera_movements.name: Wigglegram
camera_movements.description: A rapid multi-camera technique that creates the illusion of scene vibration or parallax wobble, producing an energetic, physically immersive visual effect.

camera_movements.name: Worms-Eye
camera_movements.description: A low camera angle positioned at ground level looking upward at subjects, creating the perspective of viewing the world from below as a small creature or child would.

camera_movements.name: X-Ray
camera_movements.description: The X-Ray technique creates skeletal or ghostly visual effects resembling X-ray imaging through post-production effects, emphasizing hidden or internal elements with an eerie aesthetic.

camera_movements.name: Zoetrope
camera_movements.description: A cylindrical device with sequential images on its inner surface that, when spun rapidly, creates a motion illusion through persistence of vision as viewers watch through side slits.

camera_movements.name: Zoom
camera_movements.description: A camera technique that adjusts lens focal length to create the illusion of moving closer to or farther from the subject, used to emphasize details and shift perspective.

lighting.name: Volumetric Light Rays Through Atmospheric Haze

lighting.name: Diffused Scandinavian Overcast
lighting.description: Ultra-soft, wraparound shadowless illumination simulating thick overcast cloud cover, producing flattering skin tones and muted naturalistic depth.

lighting.name: Venetian Blind Shadow Slices (Film Noir)
lighting.description: Harsh directional sunlight or neon slicing through window louvers, painting stark horizontal shadow stripes across the subject's face.

lighting.name: Stark Silhouette with Razor Rim Light
lighting.description: Subject positioned directly against an intensely luminous background, rendering their body as an ink-black silhouette with a razor-thin glowing rim.

lighting.name: Subterranean Bioluminescent Glow
lighting.description: Ethereal glow emanating organically from glowing moss, alien flora, or deep-sea organisms, casting soft phosphorescent reflections across wet stone.

lighting.name: Pristine High-Key Commercial Fill
lighting.description: Bright, completely shadowless commercial lighting with massive octabox fill, radiant skin reflections, and luminous clean environments.

lighting.name: Solitary Overhead Tungsten Spotlight
lighting.description: A single bare tungsten bulb suspended in a pitch-black industrial space, casting deep dramatic shadows downward under brow and chin.

lighting.name: Golden Hour Low-Angle Lens Flare
lighting.description: Raking horizontal sunlight from a setting sun striking lens glass directly, creating golden halation, long dramatic shadows, and honey-toned rim lighting.

lighting.name: Clinical Institutional Fluorescent
lighting.description: Harsh overhead fluorescent tubes in hospital corridors or subways, imparting sterile institutional coldness and pale greenish shadows.

lighting.name: Nocturnal Sodium Vapor Amber
lighting.description: Dirty orange-yellow glow from highway sodium vapor lamps cutting through nighttime mist, creating heavy industrial melancholy.
